It is by will alone I set my analysis in motion. I have computed the failure vectors. They are... numerous.

## Critical Severity

**Lines 97-98, 113-114, 131-133, 149-150, 171, 187-189** - SQL Injection
```go
query := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = %s", orderID)
```
The Harkonnen need not breach your walls when you leave the gate unlocked. String concatenation in SQL queries permits arbitrary command execution. An attacker submits `1; DROP TABLE orders;--` and your database becomes a smoking crater.

**Fix:** Parameterized queries exclusively. `s.db.QueryRow("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ?", orderID)`

**Line 81** - Plaintext Credit Card Storage
```go
"INSERT INTO orders ... credit_card) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)"
```
PCI-DSS violation. You store weapon-grade financial data unencrypted. The Spacing Guild would revoke your commerce license. Never store full card numbers. Use tokenization.

## High Severity

**Lines 45, 54-56, 63-65, 79-83** - Missing Error Handling
```go
json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&order)  // Error ignored
resp, _ := http.Get(...)                 // Error ignored
```
You check nothing. Decode failures, network timeouts, nil responses—all proceed as if successful. When `resp` is nil on line 67, your service panics accessing `resp.StatusCode`.

**Lines 70-77** - Fire-and-Forget Goroutines for Critical Operations
```go
go func(i Item) {
    http.Post(...)  // Inventory reservation—no error handling
}(item)
```
Payment succeeds. Inventory reservation fails silently. Customer's order "completes" but items were never reserved. Race condition: response sends before inventory confirms.

**Line 182-185** - Refund Authorization Bypass
No validation that `req.Amount <= order.Total`. An attacker requests $10,000 refund on a $50 order.

## Medium Severity

**Line 86** - Cache Without Mutex
```go
s.cache[strconv.FormatInt(order.ID, 10)] = &order
```
`cacheMutex` exists but isn't used during writes. Concurrent requests corrupt the map. Lines 94, 119, 127 exhibit the same defect.

**Lines 47-50** - Float for Currency
```go
total += item.Price * float64(item.Quantity)
```
0.1 + 0.2 ≠ 0.3 in floating point. Use integer cents or decimal types. Trust is a vulnerability; IEEE 754 confirms this.

**Lines 139-146** - Loop Variable Capture
```go
go func() {
    // productID and quantity captured by reference
}()
```
All goroutines see the final loop iteration values. Inventory release requests become duplicates of the last item.

**Lines 195-198** - Credit Card Exposure in Export
Empty string causes panic: `creditCard[len(creditCard)-4:]` on empty card. Also, exporting card data at all violates PCI requirements.

## Low Severity

**Line 205** - No rows.Close() calls. Resource leaks accumulate under load.

**No context propagation.** External API calls have no timeouts. A slow payment API blocks your workers indefinitely.
